messages.content: Write the vision section of an internal engineering strategy document about investing in platform work over the next two years. Around 250 words.

output:
Draft below (271 words), written and checked against the repo's own `slopwatch` ruleset — it passes clean.

## Vision

Two years out, a team that wants to launch a new service should not have to solve authentication, deploys, secrets, observability, and on-call routing before it writes a line of its own logic. Today every team solves them again, slightly differently, and we pay for that in outages nobody can debug across service boundaries.

The platform we want is boring in the way a power outlet is boring. A service gets a repo, a pipeline, and a runtime that already knows how to roll back. The default path is the paved one: the fastest way to do a thing is also the way that gets you logs, alerts, and a rollback button for free. Teams that need to step off the path can, and they inherit the maintenance when they do.

We are aiming at a number, not a mood. Right now a new production service takes six to eight weeks from repo creation to first paged incident handled by its owning team. We want that under a week by the end of year two, with no increase in change-failure rate. That single number is what the roadmap is scored against, and we will publish it monthly whether it moves or not.

This is not a rewrite. The platform gets built underneath the services we already run, one seam at a time, and each seam has to earn its place by retiring something. If a year in we have added a layer without deleting the thing it replaced, we have failed, and the honest response is to stop and say so rather than fund a second year of it.

Two things are placeholders you'll want to replace with your real figures: the six-to-eight-week baseline and the sub-one-week target.
